title: Interpret a rare positive alarm
scope: One binary observation with specified sensitivity and false-positive rate

items.prompt: A population has fault prevalence 1%. Sensitivity is 90%; the false-positive rate on nonfaulty cases is 5%. Given ONE positive result, compute P(fault | positive), as a probability, not a percentage.
items.solution: Use p·0.9/[p·0.9+(1−p)·0.05]=2/13. A count table gives the same ratio; sensitivity alone is not the posterior.
hints: Identify the requested quantity and its units before calculating.
